items.title: Puzzled by law student's answers, Allahabad HC asks Law Commission to examine standards of legal education
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently asked the Law Commission of India to consider examining broader issues relating to the standards of legal education in India and prepare a report to suggest appropriate reforms. Justice Vinod Diwakar said legal education constitutes the foundation of the justice delivery system and any substantial decline in academic standards at the institutional level affects not merely the legal profession but the administration of justice itself. "Law Commission of India may consider examining the broader questions relating to the standards of legal education in the country, and may prepare a report thereon should it consider such a course appropriate," the Court said on July 17. The Court also asked the Bar Council of India (BCI) to consider whether the standards of legal education are commensurate with the object for which they are prescribed. It also asked BCI to examine whether the existing mechanism for the grant of approval to institutions imparting legal education requires strengthening to compete with globally competitive legal education standards. items.title: Two Indias, one judiciary: The uneven rise of virtual courts
items.summary: On a Tuesday morning in a Bengaluru courtroom, a witness deposes over a crisp video link while the bench pulls up shared documents on a connected screen without missing a beat. 400 kilometres away, in a district court in Bihar, an identical hearing is far likelier to be adjourned - not because the law demands it, but because the internet connection will not hold, the webcam allotted to that court has been “borrowed” by another bench, or the one working laptop meant for virtual hearings is elsewhere that day. This is the quiet contradiction sitting at the heart of India’s e-courts story: a judiciary that speaks fluently of digital transformation in its policy papers, yet delivers it at wildly different speeds depending on the pin code of the litigant. The architecture for change has existed for nearly 2 decades. The e-Committee of the Supreme Court of India , working with the Department of Justice under the e-Courts Mission Mode Project, has pushed the system through three phases of digitisation. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday declined relief to five advocates who alleged they were targeted with police action after appearing in court against a real estate developer. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana Senior Advocate Devadatt Kamat , appearing for the lawyers, told the Court that all five were practising advocates who had appeared against the developer, and alleged that the Pune Police Commissioner was 'hand in glove with him'. Kamat told the Court that one of the lawyers was arrested after nearly 200 people barged into his house at 1:50 am, before any FIR had even been registered against him, and that he remained in custody for 40 days before the Bombay High Court granted him relief. “I was arrested after nearly 200 people barged into my house at 1.50 a.m. There was no FIR at that point. items.title: Why are job aspirants in Jharkhand angry? JPSC-JSSC protest enters 14th day
items.summary: The protest by state service aspirants in Jharkhand, alleging irregularities in recruitment examinations, is growing by the day. Launched on July 25 from Ranchi’s Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium under the banner of the ‘JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch’, the protest entered its 14th day on Friday. Meanwhile, political pressure on the Hemant Soren government continues to mount. The immediate trigger for the protest were the results of the 14th Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) Civil Services Preliminary Examination released on July 5. Protesters have alleged large-scale irregularities in the examination and selection process. They are demanding the cancellation of the exam and calling for a probe by the CBI or the formation of a committee comprising retired High Court judges from outside Jharkhand to investigate the matter. Since its inception, however, the movement has expanded beyond grievances related to a single exam’s results to demand comprehensive and structural reforms within the JPSC and the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC). items.title: Delhi High Court quashes criminal cases against Nestle over allegations of excess lead in Maggi
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently quashed criminal proceedings against Nestlé India Limited and its distributors in the 2015 Maggi noodles controversy, which began after food safety authorities alleged that samples of the popular instant noodles contained lead beyond the permissible limit [Dharmendra Hansraj Kotak & Ors v. State of Delhi & Anr] . In the August 6 judgment, Justice Madhu Jain held that the cases should not continue because subsequent court-supervised scientific testing found the lead content to be within the prescribed limit. "This Court is of the considered view that permitting the present prosecutions to continue would serve no useful purpose. The continuation of the complaints would merely compel the petitioners to undergo a protracted criminal trial despite the very foundation of the prosecution having substantially eroded," observed the Court.
